reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: International AI rules and governance
themes.definition: Calls for, or discussion of, international rules, norms, legal frameworks, standards, treaties or cooperative mechanisms to govern AI, including arguments that governance must keep pace with AI and must balance innovation with protection.
themes.inclusion: Passages urging common/binding/global rules, regulation, guardrails, norms, principles or multilateral cooperation on AI; references to non-UN governance initiatives (G7 Hiroshima Process, G20, AI safety summits, GPAI) as governance.
themes.exclusion: Purely national regulation (AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY); UN-specific bodies and processes (AI_UN_ROLE); demands centred on developing countries' voice in rule-making (AI_INCLUSIVE_GOVERNANCE); rejection of international governance (AI_GOVERNANCE_SKEPTICISM); weapons-specific rules (AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS).
themes.boundary_cases: A passage calling for global rules through the UN can take both AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE and AI_UN_ROLE. Generic 'responsible AI' wording without any governance mechanism or call for rules is coded here only if it addresses how AI should be governed collectively.

examples.quote: without a joint pact for the future, no country or group of countries will have the potential to offer or implement responses to those challenges alone

themes.label: UN bodies and processes on AI
themes.definition: References to the UN system's role on AI: the Secretary-General's advisory body, Tech Envoy, Global Digital Compact, Pact for the Future, Independent International Scientific Panel on AI, Global Dialogue on AI Governance, GA/Security Council agenda items, UNESCO initiatives, or the UN using AI for its own work.
themes.inclusion: Passages supporting, criticising, leading or proposing UN AI bodies, resolutions, processes or agenda items; the UN as the central forum for AI decisions; AI to make the UN more efficient.
themes.exclusion: International governance calls that do not mention the UN system or its instruments (AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
themes.boundary_cases: Criticism that the UN lags or is bypassed counts here when it calls for a UN role; outright rejection of a UN role is AI_GOVERNANCE_SKEPTICISM.

examples.quote: How we address AI together is one of the clearest tests whether we have the strength and the will to build a United Nations for today's world.

themes.label: Military AI and autonomous weapons
themes.definition: AI in warfare, weapons and strategic security: lethal autonomous weapons systems, military targeting, AI in nuclear command and escalation, and calls for rules, bans or human control over military AI.
themes.inclusion: Passages on autonomous weapons, machines deciding life and death, AI on the battlefield, military AI norms or treaties, AI as a strategic/arms-control risk alongside nuclear, cyber and space.
themes.exclusion: Non-military AI safety or loss-of-control risks (AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL); criminal or terrorist misuse and cyberattacks (AI_CYBER_SECURITY); AI used to support arms-control verification or peace (AI_PEACE_APPLICATIONS).
themes.boundary_cases: Human control of weapons is coded here, not AI_HUMAN_CONTROL. A list of threats merely naming 'AI' next to war is AI_THREAT_LIST_MENTION unless military use of AI is stated.

examples.quote: stepping back from creating killing machines — lethal autonomous weapons systems — where an algorithm decides in a split second who lives and who dies

themes.label: Frontier AI safety and loss of control
themes.definition: Technical and catastrophic AI risks: frontier model safety, misalignment, superintelligence, loss of control, uncontrolled or ungoverned AI as a survival or existential threat, and safety testing before release.
themes.inclusion: Passages warning of AI escaping human control, existential or species-level risk, superintelligence, safety requirements for the most capable models.
themes.exclusion: Military uses (AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS); general normative insistence that humans stay in charge without a safety-risk claim (AI_HUMAN_CONTROL); disinformation or crime (their own codes).
themes.boundary_cases: A brief 'uncontrolled use of AI' warning with no catastrophic or technical safety content goes to AI_OPPORTUNITY_RISK_DUALITY or AI_THREAT_LIST_MENTION.

themes.label: Human agency, control and accountability
themes.definition: Normative insistence that humans remain in control of AI and responsible for AI-assisted decisions, that people stay subjects rather than objects of algorithms, and that human judgment, autonomy and legal accountability be preserved.
themes.inclusion: Passages saying technology must remain under human control, humans must be masters of AI, decisions must stay with accountable people, or warning against outsourcing human thought and free will to machines.
themes.exclusion: Human control of weapons (AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS); catastrophic loss-of-control risk (AI_SAFETY_EXISTENTIAL); broad human rights and ethics language without the control/agency claim (AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS).
themes.boundary_cases: 'Human-centred AI' alone is AI_HUMAN_RIGHTS_ETHICS; it is coded here only when human control, decision authority or accountability is explicit.

examples.quote: Technology must remain under human control. Responsibility must always be owned by us, by humans.

themes.label: Human rights, ethics and democracy
themes.definition: AI framed through human rights, dignity, ethics, privacy, surveillance, human-centred design and democratic values, including risks of repression, algorithmic control of citizens and erosion of democratic accountability.
themes.inclusion: Passages calling for human-centred, rights-based or ethical AI, protection of privacy and freedoms, warning of AI surveillance or repression, or tying AI to democracy and accountability.
themes.exclusion: Discrimination, stereotypes and cultural/linguistic exclusion (AI_BIAS_CULTURAL_DIVERSITY); children specifically (AI_CHILD_PROTECTION); disinformation (AI_DISINFORMATION).
themes.boundary_cases: Ethics invoked as part of a call for international rules takes both this code and AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: We have to make sure that our human-centric approach applies online and offline.

themes.label: Disinformation and information integrity
themes.definition: AI-enabled misinformation, disinformation, deepfakes, manipulation of public opinion, election interference and threats to information integrity.
themes.inclusion: Passages linking AI to fake content, deepfakes, propaganda, manipulated elections or the erosion of shared facts.
themes.exclusion: Hate speech and stereotypes without a falsehood claim (AI_BIAS_CULTURAL_DIVERSITY); cybercrime (AI_CYBER_SECURITY).
themes.boundary_cases: A list naming 'artificial intelligence' and 'disinformation' as separate items does not link them; code AI_THREAT_LIST_MENTION unless the text connects AI to disinformation.

examples.quote: Latvia has meaningful experience in building resilience to disinformation and promoting media literacy.

themes.label: Cyber threats, crime and terrorist misuse
themes.definition: AI misuse by criminals, terrorists or hostile actors: cyberattacks, cybercrime, attacks on critical infrastructure, online crime, and AI within international information-security frameworks.
themes.inclusion: Passages on AI-enabled cyberattacks, fraud, trafficking, terrorism or hybrid threats, and on cybercrime cooperation covering AI.
themes.exclusion: State military use of AI in warfare (AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS); disinformation (AI_DISINFORMATION).
themes.boundary_cases: Passages that discuss only cyberspace or new technologies without naming AI are not AI evidence.

examples.quote: developing generally acceptable approaches to regulating the digital arena and understanding the processes related to the development of artificial intelligence

themes.label: AI divide and equitable access
themes.definition: Inequality in access to AI and its benefits between and within countries: risks of a new AI divide, North-South gaps, developing countries as passive consumers, and calls to share AI benefits with all.
themes.inclusion: Passages warning AI will widen gaps or leave countries behind, demanding equitable access or benefit-sharing, or envisioning AI for all.
themes.exclusion: Concrete support measures such as training, funding or technology transfer (AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING); rule-making voice (AI_INCLUSIVE_GOVERNANCE); concentration of power in firms or states (AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION).
themes.boundary_cases: When a passage states both the divide and a remedy (e.g. capacity building), apply both codes.

examples.quote: New and emerging technologies like artificial intelligence and quantum computing are racing ahead, leaving many of us behind.

themes.label: Jobs, labour and economic transformation
themes.definition: Effects of AI on employment, work, productivity, wages and the economy, including job displacement and workforce transition.
themes.inclusion: Passages on AI replacing or transforming jobs, making people economically unnecessary, raising productivity or reshaping economies.
themes.exclusion: Wealth or power concentration among firms/states (AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION); national investment showcases (AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY).
themes.boundary_cases: Skills training responding to job disruption takes this code and AI_YOUTH_EDUCATION or AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING as applicable.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence is already changing the economy, education, medicine, security, the labor market, and the way states function.

themes.label: Youth, education and skills
themes.definition: AI in relation to young people, schools and education: preparing youth for AI, AI literacy, AI in teaching, and disruptions such as plagiarism.
themes.inclusion: Passages about equipping youth with AI skills, AI's effect on learning or schools, or generative AI disrupting education.
themes.exclusion: Child online safety and exploitation (AI_CHILD_PROTECTION); international capacity-building programmes (AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING).
themes.boundary_cases: Youth employment effects of AI can take this code and AI_ECONOMY_LABOR.

examples.quote: And artificial intelligence will increasingly shape those possibilities.

themes.label: National AI strategy and achievements
themes.definition: A speaker's own country's AI strategies, investments, programmes, regulation, pilots, institutions, talent and leadership claims, including domestic regulatory approaches such as sandboxes.
themes.inclusion: Passages describing national AI plans, investments, data centres, public-service pilots, national AI laws or sandboxes, or claims of national AI leadership or hosting AI events and centres.
themes.exclusion: International cooperation offered to others (AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING); calls for international rules (AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE).
themes.boundary_cases: Hosting a UN/UNESCO AI centre takes this code and AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: joined the Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence and adopted a development strategy in that area back in 2019

themes.label: Power concentration, dependence and sovereignty
themes.definition: Concern that AI power, data, compute and wealth are concentrated in a few companies or countries, creating dependence, domination or new hierarchies, and claims to digital sovereignty, national AI models or public rather than oligarchic control.
themes.inclusion: Passages about big tech or tech oligarchs, monopolies, distrust of corporate self-regulation, technological dependence, AI as a tool of domination or neo-colonialism, and sovereign AI capacity.
themes.exclusion: Access gaps without a power/control claim (AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE); strategic competition between great powers (AI_GEOPOLITICAL_RIVALRY); rule-making exclusion (AI_INCLUSIVE_GOVERNANCE).
themes.boundary_cases: Anti-capitalist framing of AI as a systemic threat is coded here when it centres on concentrated control or wealth.

examples.quote: Cooperation must therefore create capabilities, not new dependencies.

themes.label: Geopolitical competition and AI race
themes.definition: AI as an arena of strategic competition between powers: the AI race, technological leadership, great-power rivalry, supply-chain conflict over chips, and AI as strategic infrastructure shaping world order.
themes.inclusion: Passages framing AI as a race to win or lead, a driver of rivalry, fragmentation or a new arms race, or dependent on contested chip supply chains.
themes.exclusion: Concentration in companies or domination claims (AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION); military uses (AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS).
themes.boundary_cases: A call for rules rather than a race takes this code and AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: technological capability does not automatically produce political wisdom

themes.label: AI as both promise and peril
themes.definition: Explicit framing of AI as double-edged: great opportunity alongside serious risk, a neutral tool whose effects depend on use, or public fears to be answered with reassurance.
themes.inclusion: Passages that pair AI's benefits with its dangers, call it a double-edged sword, or state that its impact depends on human choices.
themes.exclusion: Passages that discuss only a specific risk or only a benefit (use the specific code).
themes.boundary_cases: Duality language that leads directly into a governance call takes both this code and AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: It can bring enormous benefits to humanity, it can also deepen existing inequalities enable new forms of manipulation, and create security risks

themes.label: AI listed among technologies
themes.definition: AI named only briefly in a neutral or positive list of technologies, trends or national strengths, without further discussion of AI itself.
themes.inclusion: Passages where 'artificial intelligence' appears alongside other technologies (robotics, big data, quantum, biotech) with no AI-specific claim.
themes.exclusion: AI listed among threats or crises (AI_THREAT_LIST_MENTION); any passage with an AI-specific claim (use the substantive code).
themes.boundary_cases: A list plus one AI-specific sentence should receive the substantive code instead of, or in addition to, this code.

examples.quote: Some others, although of newer date, such as artificial intelligence, are already causing major changes in our lives.

themes.label: AI listed among threats or crises
themes.definition: AI named briefly within a catalogue of global challenges, threats or citizen worries (conflict, climate, pandemics, disinformation, cost of living) without elaboration of the AI risk itself.
themes.inclusion: Passages where AI or 'unregulated AI' is one item in a list of crises, dangers or public concerns, or noted as neglected on a crowded agenda.
themes.exclusion: Passages that explain how AI causes the harm (use the specific risk code); neutral technology lists (AI_TECH_LIST_MENTION).
themes.boundary_cases: If the passage says AI is a threat and names a mechanism (e.g. weapons, disinformation), use that mechanism's code.

examples.quote: rising inequality or even the unchecked rise of artificial intelligence, those challenges jeopardize our present and our future

value.rationale: Consolidated 42 proposals into 17 codes of a shared multilabel codebook. Merged: AI_GLOBAL_CHALLENGES_LIST -> AI_THREAT_LIST_MENTION (1); AI_HUMAN_CONTROL_OVERSIGHT -> AI_HUMAN_CONTROL (1); AI_INFORMATION_SECURITY_REGULATION -> AI_CYBER_SECURITY (1); AI_REGULATORY_INNOVATION -> AI_NATIONAL_STRATEGY (1); AI_TECH_VS_POLITICAL_ORDER -> AI_GEOPOLITICAL_RIVALRY (1). Distinct minority concepts are kept as separate codes (e.g. governance scepticism, inclusive rule-making, resource footprint, bias and cultural diversity, peace applications). Mention is not endorsement.
